lead_profile_text: Existing property looking for higher return
stl_goal: Escape the HMO management burden and maximise income remotely (190 miles away, based in Southampton) after a nightmare tenant caused a court order and severe property damage
property_situation: Five-bed HMO owned since October 2021; council ruled the fifth room too small for occupancy so it was converted to a kitchenette. A tenant caused a court order and left the house badly damaged; property is now undergoing a full refurb (kitchen, four en-suites, carpets, storm-damaged room) before it can be listed as a short-let.
property_type: 4-bed en-suite house (converted from a 5-bed HMO, 5th room now an upstairs kitchenette)
primary_blocker: Refurbishment timeline — kitchen and four en-suites still to be completed, no fixed completion date given, so follow-up is refurb-driven rather than calendar-driven

delay_signals.trigger_phrase: We'll have staging costs as well, won't you?
delay_signals.context: Property is mid-refurb: furniture cleared out after storm damage, kitchen being refurbished, four en-suites to be re-clad/gutted, carpets needed. Raj is still deciding whether to supply washing machine/fridge freezer himself or wait for Stayful staging. No fixed date given for refurb completion.

green_light_signals.trigger_phrase: That's the final stop. No, he had more. No, we're not doing it.
green_light_signals.context: Raj is fully done with the HMO/self-management model after a tenant required a court order and trashed the house; actively wants a professional management company to take over.

green_light_signals.trigger_phrase: We bought a five bed HMO first October 2021.
green_light_signals.context: Property is already owned outright since 2021 with no pending purchase or sale — no external transactional gate on proceeding, only the refurb.

green_light_signals.trigger_phrase: I'll send you now for, like, very soon.
green_light_signals.context: Raj began sending laser-measured floor plans and photos during the call itself and asked directly what to do next to pursue it further, showing active momentum on the parts within his control.

meeting_flow.opening_phrase: I thought I'd just start by just understanding a bit more about your current situation with the property.
rapport_topics: Family interruptions (son's friend visiting, son needing a football pump)
Wife's new Airbnb-cleaning business prompting Raj to consider short-lets
meeting_flow.pivot_to_business: Once you've got a management company in place and our service in place, I think the real hassle factor in terms of day-to-day market is going to be very similar. So the real question is which one's going to make more revenue.
meeting_flow.income_intro: So net revenues, this is what you can expect as a payout each month. There's about 3,700 pound per month.
meeting_flow.how_it_works_transition: You're not allowed to have cameras inside the property. But we already have a vetting process for guests. So just give you a bit of a guide of what that is like or what that process is.
meeting_flow.pre_close_setup: Let's just get the nuts and bolts of it. I mean, I'm pretty keen to go with you because I think, you know, you've done proper forecasting already.
meeting_flow.close_phrase: I'll send a sort of like an outline estimated like setup costs as well and I'll send our agreements so you can have a read of the terms as well and stuff like that. And then yeah, we can reconvene.

lead_responses.zac_responded_with: We normally would say this is within a sort of 10% accuracy range. It's very rare I'll have it below 10%.
lead_responses.lead_follow_up: So you're saying that there's definitely enough demand there.

lead_responses.what_lead_said: If they're contractors, they're probably going to be Monday to Friday and going back home — weekends, can anything be done?
lead_responses.zac_responded_with: You'll still get weekends — everywhere in the country will have a level of leisure demand, not just business-to-business. Figures are based on 12 comparable properties of similar size and spec within about 8km.

lead_responses.what_lead_said: So as I don't need to be fearful that you might only cover my cost, I think 1500 pound or two thousand pound a month, it won't be as low as that.
lead_responses.zac_responded_with: It shouldn't be — nothing is saying to me that you should have a loss making month if that's what your costs are.
lead_responses.lead_follow_up: Okay, because I go, what we have is four ensuites...

lead_responses.what_lead_said: You'd love cameras to watch over people. I don't get the house in trashed again.
lead_responses.zac_responded_with: You're not allowed cameras inside, but we have a vetting process — a security deposit of around £400, ID checks reviewing guest history across platforms, and insurance cover for serious damage like a deliberate fire.
lead_responses.lead_follow_up: Okay, so they checked in, cleaner's comment. So it's closely monitored compared to any other platform. Okay, great.

conversion_gaps.gap: No fixed refurb completion date — conversion is entirely gated by Raj's own building works, not by the sales process
conversion_gaps.evidence: No fixed refurb completion date yet, so this lead is time-gated by his own building works, not by sales process — follow up is refurb-timeline-driven, not calendar-driven.
conversion_gaps.how_to_fill: Maintain light-touch WhatsApp check-ins tied to refurb milestones (kitchen done, en-suites done) rather than a fixed calendar follow-up cadence

conversion_gaps.gap: Setup quote and agreement not yet reviewed by Raj, who is price-sensitive given he is already spending heavily on the refurb itself
conversion_gaps.evidence: Genuinely price-sensitive on setup cost given he's already spending heavily on the refurb itself; he is meticulous and detail-oriented (laser-measured every room) and expected to scrutinise the setup quote and agreement closely.
conversion_gaps.how_to_fill: Send a clearly itemised setup quote emphasising Stayful charges no upfront/onboarding/photography/setup fee itself, to offset concern about stacking costs on top of his refurb spend

positive_shift_moments.what_caused_shift: Zac praised the rear side-road access for contractor vans as 'a fantastic plus'
positive_shift_moments.lead_response: Yeah — Raj continued elaborating on the access details enthusiastically, describing space for three to four transit vans

positive_shift_moments.what_caused_shift: Zac confirmed nothing indicated a loss-making month against his mortgage/cost floor
positive_shift_moments.lead_response: Okay, because I go, what we have is four ensuites — moved straight into detailed refurb planning with increased engagement

friction_moments.what_caused_friction: Zac presenting the ~£3,700/month net income figure
friction_moments.lead_response: Are you sure about that? — direct challenge to the figure
friction_moments.recovery_attempted: Zac cited the ~10% accuracy range as the basis for confidence in the number

friction_moments.what_caused_friction: Discussion of no interior cameras being allowed, raised straight after Raj referenced his HMO tenant trashing the house
friction_moments.lead_response: I don't get the house in trashed again — implicit anxiety about repeat damage without visual monitoring
friction_moments.recovery_attempted: Zac walked through the vetting process step by step: security deposit, ID/history checks, insurance cover for serious damage

opening_phrases: I thought I'd just start by just understanding a bit more about your current situation with the property.
transition_phrases: So the real question is which one's going to make more revenue.
So really you're going to send me over some information about the property.
reassurance_phrases: We normally would say this is within a sort of 10% accuracy range.
Nothing is saying to me that you should have a loss making month if that's what your costs are.
That's, yeah, that's a fantastic plus.
emphasis_phrases: Net average is about 44 [thousand], per year.
If you're at 680, this should be a very profitable property for you.
zac_language.numbers_framing: Led with the net monthly payout figure (~£3,700/month) before breaking it into seasonal range (low season £2,200-2,300, peak £5,000-5,900) and then an annualised net average (~£44k), grounding all of it in 12 comparable listings within roughly 8km and a stated ~10% accuracy range, with an explicit caveat of 10-20% below forecast in year one before reviews establish.
zac_language.objection_handling_pattern: Acknowledges the objection directly, cites underlying data (comparable count, radius, accuracy range) to substantiate the figures, then reframes toward reassurance; for risk/damage concerns, explains the vetting/insurance process point by point rather than dismissing the worry.

what_they_focused_on: Whether the income figures are credible and achievable
Guest vetting and protection against repeat property damage
Whether weekday-heavy contractor demand leaves weekends empty
Confirmation that net income reliably covers his mortgage/cost floor
what_they_needed_most: Concrete proof behind the income figures (comparable count, radius, stated accuracy range)
Reassurance the new model won't repeat the HMO damage experience he just lived through
Explicit confirmation of downside protection (no loss-making months)
profile_psychology_intersection.recommended_meeting_adjustment: For HMO-exit leads with a recent bad-tenant trauma (court order, damage), introduce the guest vetting/damage-protection process earlier in the call rather than near the close — it pre-empts his strongest emotional concern before he has to raise it himself.

action_plan_responses.s3_biggest_question: Whether the income is really achievable
